llm.summary: The skill and its runtime instructions are consistent with a local-stock assistant that calls a local backend; nothing in the bundle indicates unexpected credential requests or remote exfiltration, but there are a few small inconsistencies and operational assumptions you should be aware of before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, README and SKILL.md all describe a local FastAPI backend that serves stock data and an AI chat endpoint — this matches the provided helper scripts and documentation. However, the bundle does not include the backend/ or frontend/ code referenced repeatedly in the docs (only scripts, README, SKILL.md and examples are present). That means the skill expects a separate backend service running at http://localhost:8000 (the skill's runtime instructions assume such a server exists). This is plausible for a local integration but is an important operational mismatch to be aware of.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to query local API endpoints (GET /api/stocks, /api/limit-up-analysis, etc.), run simple troubleshooting commands (lsof, curl) and to copy/edit a .env file if needed. The included scripts make only localhost requests. There are no instructions to read arbitrary system files or to transmit data to untrusted third-party endpoints. The skill does rely on a local backend being available.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only skill). The bundle contains only docs and small helper scripts; nothing is downloaded or extracted during install. This is low risk from an installer perspective.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The registry metadata lists no required environment variables, but the README/SKILL.md reference optional environment variables (AI_PROVIDER, AI_API_KEY, AI_MODEL) and a .env.example. The AI/API key variables are reasonable for AI integration but are not declared as required in the registry metadata — an inconsistency you should verify. Also pywencai is mentioned as a data source and may require its own credentials or external network access at runtime; those credentials are not declared either. The scripts themselves do not read or exfiltrate secrets.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request permanent presence (always: false), does not declare config paths, and does not modify other skills. It operates by calling local API endpoints and does not ask to persist or escalate privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is a local-stock assistant that expects a FastAPI backend at http://localhost:8000 and will call that API for quotes, limit-up analysis, shareholder data and AI chat. Before installing: 1) Note that the bundle does NOT include the backend/frontend code referenced in the docs — you must run or trust an external/my-hosted backend for it to work. 2) The README mentions optional env vars (AI_PROVIDER, AI_API_KEY) and a .env.example — supply API keys only if you trust the backend/AI provider and understand where keys are stored. 3) Review any actual backend code (not present here) before running it locally; ensure pywencai or other data-source libraries are configured deliberately and don't require hidden credentials. 4) Because the skill calls localhost endpoints, verify there are no unintended services listening on those ports that could be targeted. If you want higher assurance, ask the author for the full backend source (or a link to a trusted repository) and confirm which environment variables are actually required and how secrets are stored.
